name: bm-v2-stress-vs-strainrate
title: Growth rheology: stress vs strain rate
claim: Imposing an equibiaxial in-plane strain rate ε̇ on the growing collagen IV network and reading the steady-state stress σ(ε̇) gives the effective viscosity η = σ/ε̇ (viscous at slow rates) and the rate at which the response turns elastic — the σ(ε̇) relation a vertex model needs.
experiment: Assemble a crosslinked network, then stretch it equibiaxially at a fixed ε̇ with the crosslink chemistry on (the growing, remodelling substrate). Sweep ε̇ over a decade and read the steady-state in-plane bond-virial stress; compute η = σ/ε̇ per rate and locate any viscous→elastic crossover.
result: FIGURE-REVIEW RECONCILIATION (2026-10-20): the earlier definitive claim — a "faithful, density-calibrated, seed-ensemble" E(ε̇) rising ≈7→11 Pa (stiffening) with τ(ε̇)≈36-51 τ — was drawn from a SINGLE seed [12345] at UN-matched total strain and is not supported. Re-running the sweep at a MATCHED total strain (ε=0.12) over 3 independent seeds (real bounded LAMMPS, 60-rod NC1-angle- stabilized network) shows σ(ε̇) nearly flat/overlapping across rates (1.24±0.29 → 1.01±0.20 → 0.99±0.37 LJ for ε̇ = 2e-3 / 6e-3 / 1.8e-2) WHILE the crosslink density falls with rate (2.00 → 1.31 → 1.04 crosslinks/rod), because a slower stretch leaves more wall-clock time for crosslink assembly. The apparent mechanical resistance is therefore CONFOUNDED by rate-dependent density, not a clean rate-stiffening signal; η_eff = σ/ε̇ falls 621 → 55 LJ·time. τ(ε̇) is not cleanly resolved at this bounded scale, so De = τ·ε̇ is not reported. A density-matched dense multi-seed sweep (Mac-mini candidate) is required to separate true rate-stiffening from the density confound and to resolve τ(ε̇).
question: What is σ(ε̇), and where does the network cross from viscous to elastic?

purpose.question: What is σ(ε̇), and where does the network cross from viscous to elastic?
purpose.mechanism: At ε̇ below the crosslink turnover rate the network remodels fast enough to flow (σ ∝ ε̇, constant η); above it, bonds cannot relax between deformation increments and the response stiffens.
purpose.expected_outcome: A viscous plateau in η at slow ε̇ and a crossover to elastic stiffening as ε̇ exceeds the turnover rate.

key_assumptions: Flat biaxial slab = the growing shell to leading order (ε̇ = Ṙ/R, R ≫ mesh).
Chemistry ON during the stretch (growing, remodelling substrate) — unlike stage 1.
Steady stress read after a settle strain; network state at each rate depends on ε̇.

report.title: Stage 2 — σ(ε̇) on the growing substrate
report.verdict: Bounded-preliminary. At a matched total strain over 3 independent seeds, the network's apparent mechanical resistance does NOT cleanly stiffen with growth rate — σ(ε̇) is flat/overlapping while crosslink density falls with rate, so the response is confounded by rate-dependent assembly time. The earlier definitive ≈7→11 Pa stiffening deliverable (single seed, un-matched strain) is retracted. A density-matched dense multi-seed sweep (Mac-mini candidate) is needed before any E(ε̇)/τ(ε̇) table is handed to the vertex model. Absolute Pa still depends on the energy-scale decision.
report.main_insight: At matched strain, σ(ε̇) tracks the (rate-dependent) crosslink density more than the rate itself — the connectivity confound must be controlled before a true rate-stiffening claim can be made.

figure_review.resolution: The study is reset to bounded-preliminary. The headline deliverable is the 3-panel v2-rheology-main (σ(ε̇), η_eff(ε̇), crosslinks/rod(ε̇)) at matched total strain over 3 seeds. The old single-seed E(ε̇)/τ(ε̇) coupling table is demoted to supplement (engineered-diagnostic) and no longer presented as validated.
figure_review.mini_candidate: Density-matched dense multi-seed σ(ε̇) sweep (hold crosslink density fixed across rates; resolve τ(ε̇) for De) — a Mac-mini candidate; bounded local compute cannot separate rate-stiffening from the density confound.

config.title: Growth rate vs apparent mechanical resistance (+ paired connectivity)
config.caption: Imposed growth rate ε̇ changes the network's apparent mechanical resistance; the paired crosslink-density readout assesses whether the response reflects turnover competition or a rate-dependent change in structure. (A) σ(ε̇) is the network BOND-VIRIAL in-plane stress (reduced LJ units) read at a MATCHED total strain ε=0.12 (σ averaged over strain ∈ [0.096, 0.12]); (B) effective viscosity η_eff = σ/ε̇; (C) crosslinks-per-rod at each rate. Error bars are 3 independent networks (seeds 11/22/33; 60-rod NC1-angle-stabilized network, chemistry ON during stretch; real bounded LAMMPS). HONEST CONCLUSION: at this bounded scale σ(ε̇) is nearly flat/overlapping across rates (1.24→1.01→0.99 LJ) WHILE crosslinks/rod falls with rate (2.00→1.31→1.04) — the apparent resistance is CONFOUNDED by rate-dependent assembly time, not a clean rate-stiffening signal. η_eff falls 621→55 LJ·time. De = τ·ε̇ is not reported because τ is not resolved at this scale. A density-matched dense multi-seed sweep (Mac-mini candidate) is required to separate true rate-stiffening from the density confound.

expert_questions: Coupling units: the E(ε̇) handed to the vertex model is in reduced units (~3–5 LJ, ≈7–11 Pa at kT/σ³≈2.2). Should the coupling pass absolute pascals (requiring the energy-scale fit) or reduced units — which does the AICS vertex model expect?

Coupling contract: which vertex-model term receives the BM — a basal surface tension, a basal friction (vertex mobility), or an elastic basal spring? This decides whether we hand over a viscosity, a modulus, or both, and over what ε̇ range the (E(ε̇), τ(ε̇)) table should span.
